extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('host') is concatenated directly into a shell command via os.system(). An attacker can inject arbitrary commands by setting host to values like '127.0.0.1; rm -rf /'.
pickle.loads() is called on user-supplied data from request.body or request.GET.get('blob') (after optional base64 decoding). pickle deserialization of untrusted data allows arbitrary code execution.

User input from request.GET.get('fragment') is concatenated into a Jinja2 Template string and rendered. This allows server-side template injection (SSTI) leading to arbitrary code execution within the Jinja2 environment.

User-supplied JSON from request.body is passed directly as a MongoDB query filter to find_one() without any sanitization. Attackers can inject operators like $where, $regex, or $ne to bypass query logic or extract unauthorized data.

lxml XML parser is configured with resolve_entities=True, load_dtd=True, and no_network=False and parses untrusted XML from request.body. This enables XXE attacks allowing file disclosure, SSRF, and denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: User input from request.GET.get('ref') is used directly to construct a file path (BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f'{ref}.json'). An attacker can traverse directories using ../ to write files outside the intended private_exports directory.

cwe: CWE-22: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')

extra.message: User-supplied SSN and credit card number values are accepted via GET parameters (request.GET.get('ssn'), request.GET.get('card')) and written to disk in a JSON file. Sensitive PII is transmitted in URL query parameters and stored with no encryption.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: SignUpForm includes a 'role' ChoiceField allowing any registrant to select any role including 'school_admin'. Combined with core/views.py:87-91 which saves and logs in the user without role restriction, this enables unauthenticated privilege escalation to full administrator.

User input from request.GET.get('lane') or request.POST.get('lane') is passed directly to django.shortcuts.redirect() without any validation. This allows open redirect attacks where users can be redirected to attacker-controlled external sites.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: The Origin request header is reflected directly in Access-Control-Allow-Origin with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials set to 'true'. This allows any website to make authenticated cross-origin requests with cookies, bypassing same-origin policy protections.

cwe: CWE-942: Permissive Cross-domain Policy with Untrusted Domains

extra.message: Security headers X-XSS-Protection and Content-Security-Policy are explicitly disabled. X-XSS-Protection is set to '0' (disabling browser XSS filtering) and Content-Security-Policy is set to empty string (disabling CSP entirely).

SSL certificate verification is explicitly disabled using ssl._create_unverified_context() when making outbound HTTPS requests. This enables man-in-the-middle attacks on the connection to the partner endpoint.

course_grade_file_096 has no authentication or authorization check (no _wrk_gate call). It is publicly accessible and exposes internal operational data including financial/payment metadata about courses.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: course_identity_ping_344 has no authentication or authorization check (no _wrk_gate call). It accepts and echoes user-controlled 'handle' and 'channel' parameters from either GET or POST to any unauthenticated user.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Default SECRET_KEY 'django-insecure-local-dev-only' is hardcoded as a fallback when the SECRET_KEY environment variable is not set. If deployed without a proper secret key, this known value compromises Django session signing, CSRF tokens, and password reset tokens.

Cookie 'portal_crumb' is set from user-supplied GET parameter 'marker' using Django's set_cookie() without explicitly setting HttpOnly, Secure, or SameSite attributes. Django defaults to httponly=False, making the cookie accessible to client-side scripts.
